thesis: AI is dominated by large pretrained Transformer models built with enormous compute and web-scale data, then aligned for use as chat assistants. Capability improves primarily through scaling, while frontier models remain expensive, closed, static and unreliable.

layers.paradigm: NVIDIA GPU clusters dominate frontier training, under acute supply shortage
layers.assumption: Frontier capability requires large accelerator clusters, with NVIDIA GPUs as the industry default.
evidence: NVIDIA H100 general availability and sustained shortage — 2023
CoWoS capacity named as the constraint — 2023

layers.paradigm: Decoder-only Transformers dominate, with grouped-query attention standard and sparsity and multimodality emerging
layers.assumption: Transformer attention remains the architecture for frontier models; gains come from sparsity, scale and multimodality rather than from replacing attention.

distribution.basis: architecture family of 7 selected frontier-scale models released 2023; every publicly described example is attention-based

layers.paradigm: Pretraining, then instruction tuning and preference optimisation
layers.assumption: Capability comes from pretraining; behaviour and alignment come from preference-based post-training on human judgements.
frontier: direct preference optimisation without a reward model

layers.paradigm: Web crawl plus curated and synthetic corpora, with legal access narrowing
layers.assumption: Enough high-quality text exists on the open web, and training on more of it reliably improves capability.
evidence: New York Times v. OpenAI filed — 2023-12
no defensible share data for this layer — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Compute-optimal pretraining, with a growing interest in overtraining small models
layers.assumption: Capability follows training compute at predictable exponents.
frontier: overtraining small models well past compute-optimal
sparse scaling at constant active compute
evidence: Llama 2 trained past compute-optimal for inference economics — 2023-07
no public source apportions frontier compute by strategy — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: 100k+ token context windows with retrieval; weights frozen after training
layers.assumption: Weights are frozen at training; anything that must persist lives outside the model, in the context window or a retrieval index.
evidence: Lost in the Middle, long-context failure modes — 2023-07
context length is a property of the paradigm, not a share of it — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Chat dominates, with IDE and inline code assistants and function calling both in wide use
layers.assumption: The primary end-user interface for general AI is conversational chat.
frontier: custom assistants and GPT-style app surfaces
evidence: no public source apportions usage across surfaces — distribution omitted

layers.paradigm: Frontier capability is concentrated; capable open weights now arrive months rather than years behind
layers.assumption: Training the best models requires capital and compute available to only a small number of organisations.
evidence: GPT-4 technical report withholding architecture and data — 2023-03

bottlenecks.name: Compute cost and availability
bottlenecks.problem: Frontier GPUs are scarce and extremely expensive; training a GPT-4-class model costs a fortune and the hardware cannot be bought quickly at any price.
evidence: H100 shortage widely reported through the year — 2023
CoWoS packaging capacity named as the supply constraint — 2023
Llama 2 trained on large A100 clusters — 2023-07

bottlenecks.name: Reliability
bottlenecks.problem: Models hallucinate and make reasoning errors, and their work cannot be trusted without a human checking it.
evidence: hallucination cited in the New York Times complaint — 2023-12

bottlenecks.name: Agency
bottlenecks.problem: Models can answer questions but cannot reliably complete long, multi-step tasks; autonomous attempts drift and fail.
evidence: AgentBench showing large gaps to human completion — 2023-08

bottlenecks.name: Inference cost and latency
bottlenecks.problem: The most capable models are expensive and relatively slow to run at scale, which limits where they can be deployed.
evidence: GPT-4 Turbo introduced at lower price and higher speed — 2023-11
llama.cpp and quantised local inference emerging in response — 2023

bottlenecks.name: Closed frontier
bottlenecks.problem: The best models are controlled through APIs. Weights, data, architecture and training method are largely inaccessible, and developers depend on a handful of providers.
evidence: GPT-4 technical report disclosing neither architecture nor data — 2023-03
Llama 2 released with a restricted commercial licence — 2023-07

bottlenecks.name: Context and memory
bottlenecks.problem: Models forget across sessions, have a finite effective context even where the window is large, and learn nothing from continued use.

bottlenecks.name: Data quality and supply
bottlenecks.problem: High-quality human-generated text is finite, noisy, duplicated and increasingly constrained by law and licensing.
evidence: New York Times v. OpenAI filed — 2023-12
Will We Run Out of Data? — 2022-10

bottlenecks.name: Customization
bottlenecks.problem: Adapting a general model to a company, domain or individual remains cumbersome and imperfect.
evidence: fine-tuning unavailable on the leading closed models — 2023
